label: Cart totals
blurb: An off-by-one, a null access and a float-money bug.

result.whatChanged: This module provides utility functions for a shopping cart, including calculating the total price, applying discount coupons, and splitting the bill.

inline.title: Off-by-one error causes crash on last iteration
inline.body: The loop condition `i <= items.length` allows `i` to equal `items.length`. At this index, `items[i]` is `undefined`, which will throw a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'price')` on every execution. Change the condition to `i < items.length` or use a `for...of` loop.
inline.suggestion: for (let i = 0; i < items.length; i++) total += items[i].price * items[i].qty;
inline.quotedCode: for (let i = 0; i <= items.length; i++) total += items[i].price * items[i].qty;

inline.title: Potential crash when `code` is undefined and NaN return for invalid coupons
inline.body: The `code` parameter is marked as optional (`code?: string`), but `code.toUpperCase()` is called without checking if `code` is defined. This will throw a `TypeError` if no coupon is provided. Additionally, if the coupon code is not found in the `coupons` record, `pct` will be `undefined`, resulting in `NaN` being returned.
inline.suggestion: if (!code) return total; const pct = coupons[code.toUpperCase()]; if (pct === undefined) return total; return total - total * (pct / 100);

inline.title: `splitBill` returns a string representation of the amount
inline.body: The `toFixed(2)` method returns a `string`, not a `number`. Callers of `splitBill` might expect a numeric value for further calculations. If a string is intended, converting it back to a number is usually preferred to avoid type mismatches in calculations.
